newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn focuses on attracting foreign investment.
newsitem.headline: Bonn focuses on attracting foreign investment.

text.p: Germany should focus on its advantages, and not just costs, in defining its international competitive position, said economics minister Guenter Rexrodt and research minister Juergen Ruettgers on Monday.
In a joint report to the cabinet, the two said international investments are often aimed at "knowledge centres" and not just countries where wage costs are low.
German firms made only 15 percent of their overseas direct investments in low-wage countries, and the rest in the U.S. and Western Europe.
But Germany must also work to make itself more attractive to foreign investors, and strive to develop research and development centres like Silicon Valley, so that production jobs will follow.
"Investment and innovation conditions must improve, so that Germany remains a first address for investors over the long term," Rexrodt said in a statement.

Foreign direct investment in Germany was only 13.9 billion marks ($9.4 billion) in 1995, up from 11.2 billion marks the year before, dwarfed by German investment abroad which totalled 48 billion marks, up from 27 billion, he said.
Germany must make better use of its advantages, such as a highly qualified labour force, solid infrastructure and broad industrial basis.
But it must also work to remove weaknesses and make itself more attractive as a target for investment, he said.
-- Terence Gallagher, Bonn newsroom, 49 228 2609750 ($ = 1.482 German Marks)
